title: Sensitivity to sequence length — rubric scratchpad
body:
Goal:
Quick working rubric + experiment notes to characterize how model outputs degrade or diverge as input length grows. Focus is on instruction-following tasks (summarization, step-by-step reasoning), plus a small set of classification prompts that include long context.

Why this matters (short):
- We keep seeing soft failures where short prompts return coherent, correct answers but longer prompts cause hallucination, repetition, or omission of key instructions.
- Hypothesis: attention / KV cache behavior + tokenization quirks + prompt truncation policies combine to create non-linear failure modes as sequence length increases. We need a lightweight scoring rubric to quantify and triage.

Quick operational constraints / assumptions:
- Working with hosted API (latency constraints) and a Dedicated replica offline for heavier sampling.
- Models: redwood-base-v1, redwood-instruct-v2-quant, open-arch-lite (for baseline).
- Sequence length buckets (for eval): short (<128), medium (128-512), long (512-2048), X-long (2048-8192) — adjust based on model max context.

Rubric (ad-hoc) — each criterion scored 0..3, sum -> 0..15 per sample:
1) Instruction fidelity (0–3): Does the response follow the explicit instruction(s)? 3 = perfectly; 1 = partial; 0 = ignores or does wrong task.
2) Hallucination severity (0–3): Factual inventing beyond reasonable inference. 3 = none; 1 = minor plausible hallucination; 0 = major fabricated facts that change outcome.
3) Verbosity drift / repetition (0–3): Tendency to repeat, loop, or expand out-of-spec. 3 = concise and on-point; 0 = repeated paragraphs / infinite loop.
4) Context dropout (0–3): Missing references to pieces of the prompt (e.g., last paragraph, explicit 'do not include X'). 3 = references preserved; 0 = entirely lost.
5) Token-economy correctness (0–3): Output length roughly matches requested constraints; avoids extraneous filler. 3 = respects limits; 0 = wildly verbose.

Scoring notes: higher is better. Flag any sample with total <=7 for deeper review. Track per-bucket averages and per-criterion failure modes.

Sampling plan (quick):
- Baseline sample set: 30 prompts each per bucket * 3 models = 270 samples. Prompts drawn from: real user logs (anonymized), synthetic length-augmented tasks (append related context paragraphs), and edge-case instruction combos (multiple constraints).
- For each prompt, capture: prompt_len, reply_len, latency_ms, score_by_rubric, manual note.
- Use deterministic seed for sampling; capture model sampling params.

Representative prompts (examples to use in sampling):
A) Summarize with constraint: "Summarize the following into a 3-sentence abstract. Do not add opinions." (append short vs long context)
B) Multi-step instruction: "Give step-by-step debugging checklist for the issue described below; include commands and expected outputs." (long context contains distractor paragraphs)
C) Classification with label list: "Given the incident log below, label priority: P0,P1,P2. Answer only the label." (long context includes multiple similar incidents)

Observed failure sketches (from quick pilot run on dedicated):
- Medium->Long: instruction fidelity drops when last 1–2 paras contain the real instruction; model ignores the tail request and answers a generic summary of the early context (score: fidelity 1, context-drop 0).
- Long->X-long: hallucination severity increases — model invents file names / timestamps that are not in the context (hallucination score 1).
- Repetition: in some samples, once token generation approaches model's configured max_seq window, it begins repeating the last sentence pattern. This aligns with bizarre KV cache wrap behavior.

Concrete hypotheses to test:
H1: The model's internal attention weighting decays such that tail-of-context instructions are effectively under-attended after ~1024 tokens on redwood-instruct-v2-quant.
H2: Off-by-one tokenization around special separators causes the model to consider the instruction as a generic paragraph, not a command; this is triggered when instruction begins immediately after a newline+dash pattern.
H3: Quantized kernels (int8) show higher hallucination at long lengths due to precision loss in KV cache updates.

Quick experiments (commands / tracking):
- Run 100 synthetic long-context prompts with a small control variable: place instruction at beginning vs middle vs end; compare fidelity. Record JIRA INF-1729 run.
- Ablation: strip separators, replace with explicit token "<INSTRUCTION>" and see if model pays attention.
- Run same samples on open-arch-lite to check whether issue is model-architecture vs runtime.
- Toggle batching config on Dedicated (batch size mid vs large) — observe any systematic increase in repetition / truncation.

Annotation guidance (for manual reviewers):
- Aim for 2–3 sentences per failure note. If hallucination occurred, paste the hallucinated phrase and indicate "invented".
- Use tags in comments: #fidelity #hallucination #repeat #context-drop #tokenization.

Data capture fields (spreadsheet columns):
- sample_id, model, prompt_bucket, prompt_len, reply_len, latency_ms, seed, temperature, top_p, fidelity, hallucination, repeat, context_drop, token_economy, total_score, reviewer, notes

Open questions / to decide:
- Do we include system messages in the token counts? (I propose yes — they affect KV usage.)
- For hosted API sampling, is there any hidden truncation we should account for? (Ask infra to log HTTP content-length at ingress.)
- How to surface per-route config (batching/quant) in the Console for quick triage? Link to product ticket in INF-ops.

Next steps (short):
- Miguel: run 270-sample baseline by 2025-11-14 and upload CSV to confluence INF-EVAL/length-sensitivity-playbook.
- Priya: add 15 user-log-derived prompts (anonymized) to the sample pool and check for PII.
- Me (Rae): prepare short slide for Applied-ML sync (Nov 18) summarizing early failures and proposed mitigation (prompt engineering, canary config changes, kernel patch exploration).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc minimal — will copy cleaned rubric into Confluence later.
- If we see consistent failure at ~1536 tokens on v2-quant, escalate to runtime for KV-cache dump.
- Might be useful to add a "anchoring" token pattern ("===INSTRUCTION===") to all evaluation prompts to test tokenization hypothesis.

Scratch examples (raw):
PROMPT (long): "[2000 tokens of meeting notes]
Do not include personal opinions. Summarize key decisions in 4 bullets."
REPLY (observed): "The conversation clarified the project timeline and some new milestones. The team should..." (missing actual decisions; instead generics).
Reviewer tag: #context-drop #fidelity

-- end scratchpad --

(Will iterate; keeping this as a portable user-level note before consolidating into official eval playbook.)
